thread:
jonathan: noticed a regression in canary after yesterday's UX rollout. initial paint for dashboard widgets now ~1.8s vs 0.6s.
jonathan: looks like redux store is being rehydrated a few times per route change, causing bundle eval and multiple fetches.
maria: any reproducer steps?
jonathan: go to /dash/org/123, open timeline, then switch to reports tab. repeat a few times. network shows repeated GET /api/widgets/state?v=... with different cache keys.
kevin: can you paste the network waterfall? also which bundle chunk is re-evaluating?
jonathan: attaching snippet:
```
GET /api/widgets/state?id=org-123&v=1748882222 200 120ms
GET /api/widgets/state?id=org-123&v=1748882223 200 130ms
main.f8a9.js eval 0.9s (re-eval)
```
alyssa: hmm looks like route-change is not cancelling previous fetches and we have a stale hydration path that resets the store. maybe lazy loaded reducer is double-registering.
maria: we rolled the canary to 30% yesterday at 18:10 UTC, could be rollout UX fallback logic.
kevin: suspect the lazy reducer infra keying changed: we used to key by route id, new UX uses route+variant -> mismatched cleanup.
jonathan: repro on local with canary flag OFF vs ON: with ON we get double fetches and the main bundle eval is much higher.
alyssa: temporary mitigation: can we add a fast guard in route handler to debounce fetches and early-return if there's an ongoing fetch for same resource?
kevin: yes, I'll open a quick PR with a per-route mutex + abort controller for fetches.
maria: assign to kevin, mark rollback ready if perf doesn't recover in 30m. ping deploy-bot when PR merged.
deploy-bot: noted. canary traffic set to 10% paused. will resume on manual confirm.
jonathan: thanks, will run perf check and post numbers. keeping an eye on telemetry for LCP and handler durations.
kevin: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3123 -- adds debounce and fixes reducer unregister. running canary in staging now.
jonathan: staging looks good, initial paint down to ~0.7s. will promote to canary if no regressions in 15m.
alyssa: also adding an evaluation metric to telemetry to catch repeated fetch patterns (counter per route per session).
maria: good call. follow-up issue for a deeper root cause investigation: reducer keying + rollout UX design.
jonathan: creating the issue now and will link to PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
